high.title: Stock exchange newcomer surges 60% in 1 week, HOSE immediately issues request
high.summary: After the May 28 trading session closed, Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange (HOSE) issued a request for explanation regarding AAN stock's price hitting ceiling limit for 5 consecutive sessions from May 22-28, 2026. A An Food Company's 65 million shares officially debuted on HOSE on May 22 with reference price of 15,000 VND/share. Since then, AAN maintained purple color (ceiling limit) for 5 consecutive sessions, climbing to 23,450 VND/share - a surge of over 56% in just one week. Market cap reached 1,524 billion VND. This dramatic price movement on a newly listed stock raises market manipulation concerns and highlights the volatility risk in Vietnamese equities. Investors should monitor HOSE's investigation response and any potential trading restrictions.

high.title: State Bank speaks out on Vinhomes' gold-for-property exchange program
high.summary: The State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) has required Vinhomes to ensure compliance with all relevant laws when implementing gold-related real estate programs, including the Law on Credit Institutions, Foreign Exchange Ordinance, and real estate business regulations. SBV emphasized the government's consistent policy to encourage converting gold resources for economic development while limiting gold hoarding and speculation. The central bank stressed that gold should not be used as payment method and warned against activities that could negatively impact markets or state management. This intervention signals regulatory concern about unconventional payment methods and could impact VHM stock and broader real estate sector sentiment.

high.title: One bank stock hit by massive foreign selling of nearly 2,000 billion VND in late May
high.summary: In the final week of May (25-29), VN-Index declined 13.64 points (-0.73%) to close at 1,863.49 as selling pressure intensified. Foreign investors continued massive net selling of 5,118 billion VND across the market, with MSB bank stock being the biggest target at 1,756 billion VND net sold, followed by HPG (-549 billion) and VHM (-423 billion). On HOSE alone, foreigners net sold 5,048 billion VND. This represents one of the largest weekly foreign outflows from Vietnamese equities, particularly concerning given MSB's massive selling. The sustained foreign selling pressure suggests deteriorating sentiment toward Vietnamese banking sector and broader market, potentially signaling capital flight concerns that could pressure VND.

medium.title: Gold bar and ring prices plummet on afternoon May 28, down over 3 million VND/tael
medium.summary: Domestic gold prices crashed to 154 million VND/tael (buying price) on May 28 afternoon. SJC gold bars dropped 3.2 million VND to 154.5-157.5 million VND/tael, while gold rings fell to similar levels. This marked the third consecutive decline, totaling 3 million VND loss. International gold also declined to $4,388/ounce, reflecting global precious metals weakness.

medium.title: 1,000 Vinhomes shares now worth more than 1 tael of gold
medium.summary: VHM shares hit ceiling limit despite red market, rising nearly 80% in under 3 months to 157,700 VND/share. 1,000 VHM shares now cost 157.7 million VND, exceeding SJC gold bar prices. This mirrors VIC's performance from July 2025, when it also surpassed gold prices and subsequently gained 250% while gold only rose 30%.

medium.title: Taiwan fund wins big holding Vingroup stocks, investors still withdraw capital
medium.summary: Fubon FTSE Vietnam ETF reached near-peak performance of 27.47% since inception in March 2021, driven by Vingroup ecosystem recovery. Despite strong returns, the fund continues experiencing capital outflows from investors, highlighting disconnect between performance and investor sentiment toward Vietnamese equities.

medium.title: Dr. Can Van Luc: End of speculation era in real estate and stocks
medium.summary: BIDV's Chief Economist warns against overreaction in real estate stocks following government messaging about rental apartment development and speculation control. Dr. Luc notes Vietnam still only meets 60% of housing demand, with 40% shortage remaining, particularly in affordable segments.

medium.title: Gold prices reverse on morning May 29
medium.summary: After three consecutive decline sessions, domestic gold prices reversed higher on May 29 morning, rising 2.5 million VND/tael to 157.0-160.0 million VND/tael. International gold also bounced from $4,400/ounce lows back toward $4,500 level, testing 200-day moving average support.
